name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 17 points
Challenger Fierro has raised nothing and drawn no outside support
Incumbent Garcia holds a large fundraising edge with over $560K in outside backing
model.rationale: A strongly Democratic-leaning Houston-area seat, a renominated incumbent with roughly $1 million raised and substantial outside support, and a challenger who has reported zero fundraising leave no evidence of a competitive race, so the forecast stays with a Safe D label and a margin near the district's structural lean plus incumbent advantages.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending against Garcia, or a sudden fundraising surge from Fierro would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Houston-area district that has leaned Democratic by roughly seventeen points. She has raised nearly a million dollars and benefits from more than half a million dollars in outside support, while Republican challenger Martha Fierro has reported no fundraising and no outside spending on her behalf. No public general-election polls are available, and no professional race raters have flagged the contest as competitive.

Prediction markets put Garcia's chances at about ninety-seven percent. With the incumbent renominated, a large financial edge, and a district that has consistently favored Democrats, the race appears firmly in Democratic hands. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room for surprise, but nothing in the available evidence points to a genuine challenge. Garcia enters the final stretch as a clear favorite.
